name: Abyssal Razorshrimp
desc: Flint-shelled and segmented past counting - several of those segments being perfect duplicates. The edges are sharper than the shape carrying them has any business supporting.

name: Abyssal Shard Lobster
desc: Plated in something nearer slag than shell and cold enough to take skin off through a glove. It works its claws for a day after everything else in it has stopped.

name: Abyssal Irisfin
desc: A thousand eyes open and close in no order and never all at once. Crewmen who have gutted one report the pattern continues afterwards, on the inside.

name: Abyssal Gazer
desc: One eye the size of a fist, slotted crosswise. Crewmen who hold the stare too long report it thrashing and suffocating, which it is not doing, and cannot.

name: Abyssal Necrophyte
desc: Comes up the line decaying and stops at about half. The smell carries through a closed airlock.

name: Abyssal Aranea
desc: Neither fish nor spider and committed to both. The venom has resisted classification; medical advises against handling and the galley advises against everything else.

name: Abyssal Yellowback
desc: The one abyssal catch that looks almost ordinary. The yellow is not pigment and does not stay on the fish.

name: Abyssal Rockfish
desc: A void carried where the stomach should be. Prolonged observation eventually reveals the other side. Under no circumstances should you wave back.

name: Abyssal Ghost Manta
desc: A shadow with nothing casting it, wider than the rupture it came through. It has never completed itself and shows no sign of intending to.

name: Abyssal Ridge Clam
desc: Opens along three hinges. Reality permits two.

name: Abyssal Nautilus
desc: A chambered shell wound inward, spiralling into itself past the point where there is anywhere left to go. Each chamber holds a little of the abyss it was pulled from.

name: Abyssal Eyestar
desc: Five arms, a hundred pupils, and no agreement between them about where the centre is. Holds together while watched and comes apart when it is not. Must be watched.

name: Common Crag Crab
desc: Comes up sideways and keeps going sideways across the deck until stopped. Has the correct number of legs for a crab - unusual, considering where it came from.

name: Volturnian Crab
desc: A shell like coloured glass and equally brittle. Despite the looks and the deceptive name, the taste is vile. Commonly used for quack medicinal purposes.

name: Adolescent Pyrcrab
desc: Low, broad, and slow to commit to anything, which makes it one of the easier ones to have aboard. It runs warm to the touch, getting warmer the longer it is held.

name: Adult Pyrcrab
desc: Full-grown, and hot enough to raise blisters through a work glove. Every crewman describes a different fault in it, and each is sure the others are wrong.

name: Volturnian Lobster
desc: Blue-shelled and heavy, this pattern is near enough the true Askonian article to fetch the true price. Near enough is doing the work - the taste cannot keep up.

name: Rock Lobster
desc: Grey, plain and gripping the line rather than being gripped by it. Good eating by the standards available out here, which is not a high bar.

name: Relic Crab
desc: A broad domed shell and long tail spine give it the familiar horseshoe-crab silhouette. Chips, scoring and shallow pits across the shell match damage recorded on an already-catalogued fossil cast, down to several hairline fractures near the rim.

name: Hyperprawn
desc: Translucent, thumb-length, and arriving by the hundred. The formations they hold while drifting must not be looked at for too long.

name: Steel Pipechovies
desc: Arrives in bundles of five or six, each a straight length of dull steel with a mouth at the end. Makes for a solid replacement part in a pinch.

name: Roider Mudfish
desc: Bottom-feeder shape, bottom-feeder manner, in a medium with no bottom and no mud. Roider crews swear by them, which says more about roider crews than the fish.

name: Berylcuda
desc: Green-scaled and hard as its namesake mineral, with a barracuda's jaw grafted onto a body that might as well be a nutripaste print from a standard domain ration pack.

name: Cloudplate Tetra
desc: Plated along the back in cloud-shaped scutes, armour against pressures hyperspace has never had. Collectors pay for the ones that came through symmetrical.

name: Tiger Sailfish
desc: Trails a dorsal banner longer than the fish, striped like something that meant to be seen. The banner keeps trailing for a moment after the fish has stopped.

name: Silver Slipstreamer
desc: Silver, and already at speed, holding a heading as though the slipstream it left were still running under it. One of the few that behaves as its shape suggests.

name: Green Bass
desc: Green, blunt, and obliging. A shape with nothing stronger to settle into settles into a bass. Most survey outfits have stopped recording them.

name: Jungle Snapper
desc: Small, deep-bodied and marked in reds and greens like something raised under a canopy. Scientists are relatively certain that hyperspace features no trees, making this an irregularity.

name: Blue Ochtogon Magifin
desc: A body plated in flat panels, too regular to be chance and lit along every seam. It is not built like an animal and does not move like one.

name: Blue Tang
desc: An untroubled blue that holds longer than most colours manage - the shape appears to suit whatever has assumed it.

name: Soul Bream
desc: Broad, plain, and quiet, and the crews who bring them in will not say how the name came about. Feels occupied rather than alive.

name: Venomous Sailfish
desc: Sail-finned and patterned to warn rather than to hide, which turns out to be honest advertising for once - a claim oft confirmed by the hungry and destitute.

name: Ole' Carp
desc: Grey, slow, and uninterested. Every ship of any age has one in the logs and not one crew remembers acquiring it.

name: Credfish
desc: Flat, hard-edged, and stamped along the flank with a figure the eye keeps trying to read as a denomination. Not legal tender in any port. This has stopped nobody.

name: Long Waller
desc: Two metres of whiskered patience, feeling along a riverbed that is not there and never was. Crews find it endearing or unbearable, no ground in between.

name: Eelcat
desc: Long, whiskered, and inclined to knot itself around whatever is nearest. The knots are not knots on inspection, but no better word has been offered.

name: Bloody Damsel
desc: An orange so aggressive it reads as a warning light, and territorial about a territory that does not exist. Squares up to the drones the whole way in.

name: Goldfish
desc: Ornamental, inedible, and entirely without fight, turning up on ships whose crews have been thinking about home. Good luck to some crews and a wasted cast to the rest.

name: Bluefin Theta
desc: Rises for air in a medium that has none, over and over, at the surface of nothing. The blue along the fin is the only part of it that ever holds still.

name: Adolescent Razorspine
desc: Thin as a blade and hard as steel, yet moving as if made of flesh. Grips perfectly, throws steady, has claimed more than one life in ill-advised bets.

name: Hull Grazer
desc: A broad-headed, heavy-bodied fish with plated hide and a wide sucking mouth set beneath the skull. Loose specimens readily clamp onto ship hulls, rasping away asteroid grit and settled space dust. The armour beneath is left untouched, if cleaner than before.

name: Silver Razorspine
desc: Grown out, with a thick plate of patterned steel protecting a leathery underside. Heavy enough to deform gear rated well above it. The metal carries crude forge-marks.

name: Mossy Bass
desc: Furred green along the back with something that is not moss but feels like it. Turns itself away from the sun if left unsupervised. Tastes exactly how it looks.

name: Largemouth Bass
desc: Big, blunt, obliging, and the most logged specimen in the Sector by a wide margin. Two together are never the same size, and never wrong the same way.

name: Moiré Mackerel
desc: Its dark bars slide, split and recombine continuously across an otherwise ordinary mackerel. The pattern never settles long enough to follow; looking at it for more than a few seconds strains the eyes.

name: Marlin
desc: Long bill, long body, and equally long resentment for being caught. Bringing one in is generally the end of the work for that watch, one way or the other.

name: Pacu Pacu
desc: Blunt, flat-toothed and disconcertingly human about the mouth. The teeth are the part of the pattern that came through cleanest.

name: Perch
desc: Striped, spiny and thoroughly ordinary. Yes, completely ordinary. Yes.

name: Plume Remora
desc: Thin and blue-white, it is usually found holding position behind a drive nozzle. It is highly resistant to heat and radiation, making the scales good reactor insulation in a pinch.

name: Pomfret
desc: Silver, deep-bodied and easy to catch. Holds its shape better than most. Often a new crew's first catch and generally the only thing they remember about it.

name: Pufferfish
desc: Arrives slack and unimpressive, having concluded that the danger has passed. It has not.

name: Ballooner
desc: A pufferfish with its mind made up - inflated, spined, and declining to come back down. Cutting one open doesn't change the shape of the fish.

name: Deepwater Pufferfish
desc: Blue and already inflated on the way through the rupture, as though something down there startled it. Nothing did, as far as the instruments can say.

name: Silver Star
desc: Winged, silver, gliding on a medium with nothing to glide upon. It matches no record in any Domain database, and xeno-survey has declined to take an interest.

name: Gargantuan Waller
desc: A waller grown past all reason, heavy-headed and wrong about its own proportions. Takes two deckhands and a winch to move. Requires frequent moving between bays to account for the ever-increasing mass.

name: Nemo
desc: Banded orange and white. Sealed in a bag of water nobody aboard put it in. The bag holds, and reads as standard plasteel on analysis.

name: Curious Damsel
desc: Small, bright, and inclined to follow machinery rather than flee it. Curiosity is not on the list of things these are supposed to be capable of.

name: Flarefin Koi
desc: Fins like a flare going off, trailing light that illuminates nothing around it. Ornamental stock from a garden nobody has placed, on a world nobody has named.

name: Stinkfish
desc: The smell arrives first and outlasts the specimen by days. The compound responsible for this has never been isolated, which has not helped morale.

name: Blue Sea Tuna
desc: Big, blue, and built to cross an ocean in a place that has never held one. It makes the crossing anyway, at speed, in whatever direction it happened to be pointed.

name: Rainbow Carp
desc: Ornamental, patterned in colours the ship's screens cannot quite render. Worth more to a collector than to a galley.

name: Blind Crawler
desc: Eyeless, feeling its way along the bottom of a place with no bottom, and sounding a low note it needs water to make. It makes the note regardless, and keeps making it on the deck.

name: Red Snapper
desc: Deep red, sharp-toothed and a genuine fight. One of the few catches worth logging for its own sake.

name: Coach
desc: Small, silver, and absolutely everywhere. Named by a deckhand who found it funnier than it is, and the name went into the manifest before anyone could object.

name: Sulfur Diver
desc: Mottled yellow, reeking of sulphur, and inclined to hold position rather than run. It outlasts pursuit rather than outpacing it, which works more often than it should.

name: Storm Salmon
desc: Runs against a theoretical current, hard and in one direction, trailing charge the whole way. Nobody has established what it is running towards - or from.

name: Hammerhead
desc: A compact fish assembled in the proportions of a Hammer-class torpedo, down to the blunt low-tech casing and tail fins. Once moving, it tends to keep one heading, which is reason enough to secure the transport tank.

name: Shad
desc: Thin silver schooling stock with no school to join. It arrives alone, and conducts itself throughout as though it were among thousands.

name: Silverback
desc: Heavy through the shoulder and silver along the spine, throwing itself clear of a surface that does not exist. A hazard to the drones and occasionally to the crew.

name: Skate
desc: Flat, winged, and gliding through space with otherworldly grace. It passes over the drones rather than through them, a distinction the machinery is not equipped to appreciate.

name: Spined Loach
desc: Small, whiskered, and armed under the eye with a spine that catches on everything. More trouble than it is worth, and the trade prices it accordingly.

name: Ice Tuna
desc: Heavy, cold through, frosted along the flank, and the best eating in the catalogue by a comfortable distance. Worth every bit of the gear it costs to bring one in.

name: Vulcan Cannonfish
desc: Blunt-nosed and barrel-bodied, built to the proportions of ordnance rather than of anything that ever swam. It assumed the shape nearest to hand, and found an autocannon.

name: Weathervane
desc: Narrow and rigid, it points in the same direction through currents and handling. Compared with range data, the heading matches the nearest rupture.

name: Amberjack
desc: Fast, yellow along the tail and a long fight for its size. Sought by crews who have grown tired of bass.

name: Lantern Jack
desc: Built like an anglerfish at hauler scale, with a distress beacon for a lure. The signal is decades old but correctly formatted, and grows stronger at close range. Keep the comm link closed while hunting it.

name: The Quorum
desc: A school of roughly ten thousand silver fish. They turn together, take the hook together, and register as a single specimen. Dividing the school on deck does not change the tally, but will change the crew count.

name: Quorum Splinter
desc: A dozen silver bodies holding formation around an empty centre. Attempts to count them overwhelmingly fail, the total showing only a single fish.

name: Slipstream Moray
desc: An eel long enough to qualify as a navigation hazard, found only where the fabric is close to breaking. Nearby slipstreams curve toward it, and plotted courses update to match.

name: Shimmerclam
desc: Shut on arrival and shut since, against every tool rated for the job. The shell runs through colours it carries no pigment for.

name: Freight Clam
desc: A clam with shell halves shaped like the jaws of a freight clamp, with locking lugs around the hinge. Closed, it could pass for cargo-securing hardware. Opened, it certainly does not.

name: Lunacyte
desc: Pale and unhurried, lit from within on a cycle that matches nothing aboard. Named by a crew that watched one for a full shift, and would not afterwards explain the name.

name: Poison Jelly
desc: Dangerous at the best of times, and tends to dissolve into extremely toxic slurry once exposed to water. This pattern has wiped out more than one crew through negligence.

name: Aetherial Jelly
desc: Barely present and barely holding, a shape more suggested than built. Handled roughly it comes apart, and the pieces do not stay pieces for long.

name: Mussel
desc: Clamped shut around an object that did not make the jump to realspace. Tastes better when not reminded of this fact.

name: Deep Terror
desc: Eight arms, deep red, and a great deal better coordinated than the crew watching it. It gets into things, and it has never once been found where it was left.

name: Yellow King
desc: Carries markings that resolve, given long enough, into a stage play. Crews who read the second act are relieved of duty and locked in the brig indefinitely.

name: Undersea Bee
desc: Fist-sized, barely coherent, and arriving in swarms. They all behave as one animal, which no single one of them is built to be.

name: Mind Flayer
desc: Nothing anyone has put in front of one has ever been eaten. Crew quartered near one lose hours first, then names, then the ability to read. The specimen gains mass.

name: Crystal Aberration
desc: Faceted and rigid, lit from within in shimmering colours. The arms crackle and splinter with every movement, an ailment transferable by touch.

name: Giant Squid
desc: Deep red, long-armed and inking freely, which is a problem when the ink does not stay where it lands. Bring a bucket, something to put under the bucket, and something to put all of that into.

name: Corona Shark
desc: Mirror-skinned and unmistakably shark-shaped. It dives through the corona of its star as though hunting, though it never returns with any visible prey. Taken beyond the vicinity of its origin, it withers into a rigid, statue-like form.

name: Volley Dolphin
desc: A compact dolphin that bats floating objects back and forth with striking accuracy. Feed scoops, marker buoys and cleaning floats become playthings; tank crews learn to clear loose gear before opening the lid.

name: Egg
desc: Hyperspace does not spawn, so this is a shape with no process behind it. It has never hatched, and standing orders are not to wait around and find out.

name: Bulkhead Turtle
desc: A heavy turtle with a shell of flat machined plates bearing clean tool marks. A part number is stamped beneath the rear plate, but no available catalogue recognizes it. Handling crews use a lifting frame.

name: Larva
desc: A thing between shapes that stopped between them. Reality let it stand on the grounds that larvae are permitted to be unfinished.

name: Waterpillar
desc: Segmented and ringed, moving in a wave with nothing available to push against. A pattern common on land, which raises the question of where it came from.

name: Emmerling
desc: Named by the crew that recorded the first, and the name held for want of a competing suggestion. No template has been found for it, in Domain records or since.

name: Nav Turtle
desc: A squat turtle whose shell reads at a glance as a navigation buoy casing. It holds station without an anchor and blinks a valid registration assigned to no vessel.

name: Skelleton
desc: Reality took the skeleton and declined the rest. Misspelled on the first survey sheet and every sheet since.

name: Banana Star
desc: Five arms, yellow, curved, and jointed where arms are not jointed. Named by a crewman who has since been quietly reassigned. Extremely venomous. Tastes like banana.

name: Crusty Star
desc: Blue, rough as old plating and entirely indifferent to being caught. Carries on doing whatever it was doing the whole way up.

name: Crystal Star
desc: Rigid, faceted, and ringing faintly whenever it is set down on anything hard. It appears in safety briefings, under the handling section, as the example.

name: Leafy Star
desc: Soft-armed, and regenerating anything taken off it faster than the available material accounts for while exposed to light.

name: Scraggly Star
desc: Thin-armed, uneven, and short one point - and never the same point twice. The fabric appears to have made an accounting error here, and elected to let it stand.

name: False Dawn
desc: The sensor plot logs it as a faint star with steady parallax until the breach lights come on. At close range it is a bright jellyfish-like shape that gives off an unimaginable amount of heat and is best stored in a spare onboard reactor.

name: The Imposter
desc: At range it presents the profile, mass and transponder return of one of the Fisherman's boats. Once exposed by breach lights, the return resolves into a heavy whale-shaped body with broad flukes and a blunt head. The transponder code remains the same.
